observation.visible_scene: An outdoor round metal fire barrel set on ground scattered with snow and dark gravel. The left portion of the barrel's opening holds a pile of thin sticks and split wood with active orange-yellow flames; the right portion is covered by a perforated metal grate, on which a small silver pot/cup rests. A bent metal handle/bracket spans the middle of the opening. The framing is a fixed high-angle view throughout.
visible_changes: The flames continuously flicker, rise, lean, and change shape and brightness from frame to frame, with tongues of fire shifting position over the wood pile.
Glowing embers and reddish wood surfaces appear and dim as the fire burns.
Thin wisps of pale smoke become visible drifting near the right/center area in the later frames (roughly from t=0.23s onward), more noticeable around t=0.7-0.9s.
The wood pile, metal grate, pot, and barrel rim remain in fixed positions; no object is added, removed, or moved.
The snow and gravel background pattern stays the same, indicating no significant camera translation.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the fire was started and what fuel is present outside the visible pile.
Whether the pot is being heated or used for anything.
The continuation or outcome of the burn after the last frame, and the state before the first frame.
uncertain_details: Minor pixel-level framing differences may be handheld jitter or compression rather than deliberate camera motion; the camera is treated as essentially stationary.
The exact material/identity of the pot and the metal bracket is not confirmable from the images.
Whether the smoke is solely from the fire or influenced by wind is not determinable.
